name: P1 · Computer Literacy
description: 1 of 14 topics so far (2 sets × 20 questions): Unit 1 – Introduction to Computer. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

sets.name: 1 · What is a Computer, Categories and Types

questions.question: A computer is best described as an electronic device that:

options.A: Accepts data, processes it according to instructions, stores it and produces output
options.D: Thinks and decides on its own without instructions

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Input → process → output, with storage, all under program control.

questions.question: The word 'computer' is derived from the word 'compute', which means:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Early computers were built mainly for calculation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a computer?

options.D: It has its own intelligence (IQ) and feelings

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: A computer has zero IQ; it only follows the instructions given to it.

questions.question: The principle GIGO means:

options.B: Garbage In, Garbage Out – wrong input or instructions give wrong output
options.D: Good Input, Good Output – the computer corrects errors

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Computer errors are mostly caused by wrong data or wrong programs.

questions.question: On the basis of how they work (the type of data they handle), computers are classified as:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Size gives micro/mini/mainframe/super; purpose gives general/special.

questions.question: A car's speedometer showing speed by a moving needle is an example of an:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: It measures a continuously changing quantity.

questions.question: A machine in a hospital ICU that measures a patient's heartbeat and blood pressure (analog) and displays them as numbers (digital) is an example of a:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Hybrid computers combine analog measurement with digital processing.

questions.question: Arrange computers by size and computing power, from smallest to largest:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the fastest and most powerful.

questions.question: PARAM, India's first supercomputer series, was developed by:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: PARAM 8000 was released in 1991.

questions.question: The speed of supercomputers is usually measured in:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Modern supercomputers work in petaFLOPS and exaFLOPS.

questions.question: Large organisations such as banks and railway reservation systems, which support thousands of users at the same time, mainly use:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Mainframes handle huge volumes of transactions reliably.

questions.question: A computer built into a washing machine to control its washing cycle is called:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Embedded systems are special-purpose computers inside other devices.

questions.question: Desktop PCs, laptops, tablets and smartphones are all examples of:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: They are built around a microprocessor and are used by one person at a time.

questions.question: A computer that provides files, web pages or other services to other computers on a network is called a:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Clients request services; servers provide them.

questions.question:
Match the computer with a typical use:
a. Supercomputer
b. Mainframe
c. Microcomputer
d. Embedded computer

1. Bank transaction processing
2. Controlling a microwave oven
3. Personal work at home or office
4. Weather forecasting
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Weather forecasting needs the huge speed of supercomputers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A general-purpose computer can run many different kinds of programs.
II. A special-purpose computer is designed for one particular task.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: E.g. a PC is general-purpose; a traffic-signal controller is special-purpose.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Digital computers work with discrete values (digits).
II. Analog computers are more accurate than digital computers.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Digital computers are more accurate; analog ones work with continuous quantities.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Computers can work for long hours without loss of accuracy.
Reason (R): Computers do not suffer from tiredness or lack of concentration.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: This quality is called diligence.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A computer can decide by itself what problem to solve.
Reason (R): A computer works only according to the instructions given in a program.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Because it only follows programs, it cannot decide by itself; R shows why A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Supercomputers are used for weather forecasting.
Reason (R): Supercomputers are the smallest and cheapest computers.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: A is true because forecasting needs enormous calculation; R is false – they are the largest and costliest.

sets.name: 2 · Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software

questions.question: The only language a computer can execute directly, written in 0s and 1s, is:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: All other languages must be translated into machine language.

questions.question: Assembly language uses:

options.A: Mnemonics (short codes) such as ADD and MOV

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: An assembler translates it into machine code.

questions.question:
Match the translator with its job:
a. Compiler
b. Interpreter
c. Assembler

1. Translates and executes a high-level program line by line
2. Translates a whole high-level program at once
3. Translates assembly language to machine code
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Compilers produce a complete object program; interpreters do not.

questions.question: Which of the following is a high-level language?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: High-level languages are close to human language and machine-independent.

questions.question: 1 kilobyte (KB) is equal to:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: 2¹⁰ = 1024; 1 byte = 8 bits.

questions.question: Half a byte (4 bits) is called a:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: A byte has two nibbles.

questions.question: Arrange in increasing order of size:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Each unit is 1024 times the previous one.

questions.question: Which memory loses its contents when the power is switched off?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile; the others keep data without power.

questions.question: The BIOS program that starts a computer is usually stored in:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Software permanently stored in ROM chips is called firmware.

questions.question: Arrange in order from fastest to slowest:

options.B: CPU registers, cache memory, RAM, hard disk

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Faster memory is smaller and costlier per byte.

questions.question: A standard single-layer DVD can store about:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: A CD holds about 700 MB and a single-layer Blu-ray about 25 GB.

questions.question: Which of these is secondary (auxiliary) storage?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile and holds data permanently.

questions.question: Intel and AMD are well-known manufacturers of:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Dell, HP and Lenovo make complete computers; Microsoft makes Windows.

questions.question:
Match the software with its type:
a. Windows
b. MS Word
c. Antivirus program
d. Device driver

1. Operating system (system software)
2. Utility software
3. Application software
4. Software that lets the OS control a hardware device
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Operating systems and drivers are system software.

questions.question: Software whose source code is freely available to be studied, changed and shared, such as Linux, is called:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Windows and MS Office are proprietary (closed-source).

questions.question: Software that can be used free for a trial period, after which the user is asked to pay, is called:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Freeware is free to use without payment.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Hardware refers to the physical parts of a computer.
II. Software can work without any hardware.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Hardware and software need each other: software runs on hardware.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. ATMs and online banking are applications of computers in banking.
II. E-governance uses computers to deliver government services to citizens.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Both are common applications of computers.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Programs written in a high-level language must be translated before execution.
Reason (R): A computer can directly execute only machine language.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Compilers or interpreters convert them into machine code.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): RAM is used to store data permanently.
Reason (R): RAM is volatile memory.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Because RAM is volatile, it cannot store data permanently; R shows why A is false.
